body.heading: Words that sing the same ending
paragraphs: Some words end with the same sound, like a little echo: kit and pit, fox and box. Words like that rhyme — and rhyming is one of the first steps to reading, because ears learn to hear the parts of words.
Read these silly sentences out loud. Can you hear the echoes?

body.heading: Make your own
paragraphs: The ending sound is the magic part. Keep the ending, change the beginning: cat, bat, hat, mat, rat all live in the same rhyming family.
Now you try: what rhymes with pig? (wig, dig, big!) What rhymes with sun? (fun, run, bun!)

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Which silly sentence is your favorite? Say it three times, faster each time!
2. Invent a brand-new rhyming pair: 'A bee in a…' (tree!). Draw a picture of it.

takeaway: Rhyming words end with the same sound — hearing those echoes (kit/pit, fox/box) is a first step toward reading.
materials: Just you and this page — no materials needed
supervision: A grown-up nearby is recommended for younger readers; the think-and-talk questions work well read aloud together.

screenFreeExtension: Rhyme hunt at home: pick a word and find three things whose names rhyme with it, or invent funny ones together.
